beats.say: EthioEMR is one platform with three parts: the team's EMR, Form Studio for building forms, and an AI assistant inside the chart.
First, Form Studio. It opens from the app menu and lists every form in the EMR.
Here is the gynecology triage form in the editor, next to a live preview.
Rules are written in plain words. PV is shown only when Vaginal Bleeding is Yes.
The preview follows the rule. Choose Yes, and PV appears.
The Check looks up every concept on the server. Zero errors, so the form can be downloaded.
Now the AI assistant. It retrieves passages from Ethiopian and WHO guidelines, answers only from those passages, and cites each one.
In Help and Search, a clinician asks for the danger signs of severe malaria, then presses Ask.
The answer lists the danger signs and names its sources: the guideline and the page.
On a patient's chart, the Diagnosis Assistant. The clinician presses Speak and records the consultation in Amharic.
A speech model on this machine writes down what was said, in Amharic script. It transcribes. It does not translate.
One click sends the complaint and the patient's recent vitals to the assistant.
Back comes a ranked differential, built from the transcript, the vitals and the guidelines.
Each item links to the chart record or guideline page behind it. Nothing is written to the chart.
One platform: the team's EMR, Form Studio, and an AI assistant that cites its sources.
